content.intro: Learn asynchronous orm and external i/o through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous ORM and External I/O matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines asynchronous orm and external i/o as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

items.title: a -prefixed asynchronous QuerySet methods
items.text: Async code helps most when it can await non-blocking I/O; CPU-heavy work or blocking libraries can still stall the event loop. Test timeouts, cancellation, concurrency limits, and sync/async boundaries.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Asynchronous ORM and External I/O
content_blocks.code:
async def headlines():
    rows = []
    async for article in Article.objects.filter(is_published=True):
        rows.append(article.title)
    return rows
content_blocks.expected_output: Django supports asynchronous QuerySet iteration for compatible queries; async variants and lazy related-field access need deliberate handling.

content_blocks.troubleshooting: For Django 6.1, check the async support docs and use sync_to_async around synchronous transaction logic. The snippet assumes Article exists.
